newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says China rejects visit by its negotiator.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says China rejects visit by its negotiator.

text.p: China, which recently wined and dined dozens of Taiwanese tycoons, has rejected a visit by one of Taiwan's top bilateral negotiators, officials said on Monday.

Chang Liang-jen, vice secretary-general of the state-funded Straits Exchange Foundation, had planned to travel to China with a Taiwanese musical delegation on September 14 for a 10-day visit, a foundation official said.
"We informed the mainland's Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits that Mr Chang would visit with the delegation but it did not give approval to Mr Chang," the official said.
"They did not give a reason," she added.
The semi-official groups were formed in the early 1990s to represent the rival governments in Taipei and Beijing at the bargaining table in the absence of formal ties.
They held a landmark meeting in 1993 and a series of technical-level talks followed to discuss civilian issues.

But China suspended the talks in mid-1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui's private but high-profile visit to the United States, which Beijing said showed Taiwan wanted independence rather than reunification with the mainland.
China has declined visits by senior officials of the Taiwan foundation since mid-1995.

Despite the political impasse, an increasing number of Chinese officials made private visits to the island to promote direct shipping links and Taiwanese business leaders toured China for investment opportunities in recent months.
The latest exchange was a visit to China by Taiwan industrial leaders that included an audience with President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin.

Both sides have expressed willingness to resume the talks in recent months, but Beijing has stopped short of letting this happen, saying Taiwan should show sincerity by dropping its effort to raise a higher international profile.
China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war ended in 1949. Both sides say they want reunification, but under very different terms.
Beijing says Taiwan is not entitled to foreign ties while Taiwan insists its 21 million people have the right to a role in international society, including a seat in the United Nations.
